text: London Now. “Imagine this reader, at the click of a button, every public library in the UK is lost, destroyed, forgotten. Would you even notice this change? Well according to the Arts Council England, only 30% of the general public (aged over 16) have used public libraries in the last year. To put this in perspective, in 2006, roughly half of the adult population in the UK had used public libraries that year. This drastic decline has been often attributed to the increasing use of modern technology such as Mobile phones and ebooks, leading to less people actually needing to use a physical book. Does this mean that modern public libraries are obsolete?” … “change is inevitable and thus libraries no longer have the purpose of holding information, but rather now have a duty of providing a safe space for people to hang out, to have fun and to read.”

text: A new book revisits the years when Bombay’s working-class libraries were flourishing – Scroll. “As Bombay expanded in the late 19th century and early 20th century, it developed a strong library culture, which came to be organised along various lines – religious communities, neighbourhoods, and secular educational institutions. On the one hand, there were community-led libraries, such as the Mulla Firoz Library (established in 1830), containing books relating to Zoroastrian religion, the Jain Reading Room and Library, the Jamestji Nasarwanji Petit Fore Reading Room and Library by Parsis, the MJ Khoja Library and the Anjuman-i-Islam by Muslims. On the other hand, there were strong neighbourhood libraries, such as the Native General Library (established in 1845) in Dhobi Talao and Sr D Petit Khanda Mohalla Library in Nizampura.”

text: Staffordshire council sets out new library display rules after Pride row – A Little Bit of Stone. “Staffordshire County Council leader Martin Murray said in June that Pride events would no longer be promoted in the county’s public libraries. The announcement came as the council reviewed the use of library display space. While that review was taking place, the authority said displays not promoting the core library offer or wider council services would be paused. Thousands of people subsequently signed an online petition calling on the council to reverse any policy preventing libraries and other council services from displaying materials recognising and celebrating LGBTQ+ communities and other protected groups during awareness and heritage months. text: Library closed after rent row could become bookies – BBC. “Breck Road Library, in the Anfield area of Liverpool, has been closed since November 2025 after a rent dispute. – Distributed £1.8m in grant funding over two years benefitting more than half the library services in England. This funding supported a range of digital products and services, including virtual tours to enhance accessibility, bespoke apps for ordering books and catalogue search, website upgrades, AI tools to support access for users, events platforms and much more.
– A national brand and online presence to promote public libraries.
– User research which developed our understanding of library use and the barriers faced by new and lapsed users.
– A national website with content, videos, case studies, special collection stories, digitised archive material, a library finder map and an API-powered nationwide event listing featuring over 2,000 library events at any one time.
– An extensive database of 3,000+ libraries across the UK was developed, which included comprehensive data on location, opening times, services, accessibility and a self-service portal to manage the data.
– A LinkedIn newsletter delivered to 30,974 subscribers, plus regular drop-ins, show & tells and the Press Play digital conference in March 2024.
– Over 77% of English library services attended a LibraryOn community of practice session at least once.  
– By July 2026, the LibraryOn website had hosted 280,000 sessions since its launch, with 22% of traffic going on to explore library websites in the past 12 months.   
–  LibraryOn collaborated with 61% of English public library services to showcase the best of what libraries offer via social media activity. Marketing activity across paid ads between 2023 and 2026 created just under 23.5m impressions and 179,659 clicks to the LibraryOn website.
